text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Italian lira reenters European Exchange Rate Mechanism at rate of 990 lira per mark.

-- Saint-Gobain chairman Jean-Louis Beffa in an interview says workers' stock options schemes have helped privatised groups, adds Saint-Gobain has the means to carry on with its acquisitions policy without risking part of its capital.
-- National Assembly votes in favour of the introduction of pension funds in France.
-- Parliamentary report suggests a privatisation of Aerospatiale ahead of a planned merger with Dassault.
-- Lira re-enters European Monetary system at a rate of 990 lira to a mark.
-- Talks between truck drivers and employers end in stalemate overnight, protesters tighten blockades of towns, petrol depots and ports. Government names a mediator in the conflict.

-- Valeo chairman Noel Goutard in an interview says size of automobile sector justifies state help, but improving competitivity is necessary, adds Valeo plans to invest in the United States, South-East Asia, and Europe.
-- Pinault-Printemps-Redoute retail group relied on innovation and marketing to achieve a 20 percent growth of its profit in 1995 despite sluggish economic conditions.
-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis to meet association of pre-1910 Russian bond holders after Russian government offered them a glimpse of hope of reimbursement.
-- EU allows the lira back into its grid.
